title: Dynamic prediction of cardiovascular risk from linked primary care records in New South Wales, Australia: protocol for a retrospective prognostic modelling study
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains a leading cause of preventable morbidity and mortality. Most existing CVD prediction tools use a baseline survival modelling framework, in which each predictor is represented by a single value recorded at the start of follow-up. Although risk calculators can be re-run using updated values, these models do not explicitly use the longitudinal, irregularly recorded information in primary-care electronic medical records (EMRs). Dynamic modelling approaches have the potential to generate updated CVD risk estimates at each general practitioner (GP) encounter, supporting both risk assessment and monitoring of changes over time. This protocol outlines the development and validation of transformer-based sequence models for encounter-level prediction of 5-year CVD risk, compared with dynamic landmark survival models and benchmarked against static CVD prediction tools. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The study will use the New South Wales (NSW) Lumos linked health data asset, a large, privacy-preserving linkage of GP EMRs with hospital admissions, mortality and other administrative datasets across NSW, Australia. Eligible GP encounters will be included from 2018 onwards. The primary outcome is first fatal or non-fatal CVD event within 5 years of each eligible encounter, identified using ICD-10-AM codes in linked hospital and mortality data. Predictor variables include routinely collected demographics, chronic conditions, clinical measurements and medications, as well as healthcare utilisation patterns available at or before each encounter. Sex-specific dynamic landmark survival models (such as Cox proportional hazards models) with time-updated covariates (full and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-regularised) will be developed alongside sex-specific transformer-based sequence models, fine-tuned for 5-year risk prediction at each encounter. Internal validation will use repeated resampling for landmark survival models with patient-level and temporal separation for sequence models. Geographic transportability will be evaluated using internal-external validation across primary health networks (PHNs). Performance will be evaluated using discrimination, calibration, decision-curve analysis and subgroup analyses and will be compared with existing static predictive models. Missing-data will be imputed where necessary: a range of imputation approaches will be compared to optimise computational efficiency but also support predictive generalisability. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study is conducted under NSW Health governance arrangements with approval from the NSW Population and Health Services Research Ethics Committee (2019/ETH00660). Analyses will be performed within a secure data environment using de-identified linked data. Results will be reported in accordance with TRIPOD-AI guidance and disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, scientific conferences and policy and consumer forums.

title: Anomaly Detection in Environmental Data Using the Isolation Forest Algorithm (Case Study of the Malang Regency Environmental Agency)
abstract: Abstract In the era of government digitalization, data validity and consistency are crucial in supporting data-driven decision-making. This study aims to implement the Isolation Forest algorithm to detect anomalies in environmental sector data within a regional government institution and to evaluate its effectiveness in improving data consistency and validity. The dataset used consist of annual data on waste management from 2019 to 2024. The analysis was conducted using Phyton Programming Language with scikit-learn library. Based on the anomaly score, two anomalies were identified in the years 2021 and 2023. These findings are suspected to be caused by data entry errors, incomplete data, or inconsistencies in formatting and unit. Therefore, this approach has proven to be an efficient and automated tool for the initial validation process of sectoral data integrity. This can contribute to the improvement of government data quality.

title: Employee-AI collaboration errors and service innovation: dual pathways of error reflection and negative affective rumination
abstract: Employee-AI collaboration models are increasingly implemented in service organizations. Although such models enhance employee efficiency and service quality, errors in the collaboration process remain frequent. However, the effects of errors during human-AI collaboration on employees’ service innovation remain unclear. Drawing on the transactional theory of stress, this study investigates how employee-AI collaboration errors influence employees’ AI-enabled service innovation behavior. Based on a three-wave survey and an experiment, this study finds that when AI technology-task fit is high, employee-AI collaboration errors are more likely to trigger employees’ error reflection, which in turn facilitates their AI-enabled service innovation. In contrast, when AI technology-task fit is low, employee-AI collaboration errors tend to induce negative affective rumination, thereby undermining employees’ AI-enabled service innovation. Overall, this research extends prior literature on human-machine collaboration and service innovation while offering actionable insights for service organizations seeking to foster employees’ innovation behavior in the context of human-AI cooperation.

title: Image-text multimodal fusion for radar signal modulation recognition in open-set scenarios
abstract: Existing radar signal modulation recognition methods primarily focus on closed-set scenarios. Although recent studies have begun addressing open-set recognition, most existing methods rely on single-modal data, limiting their semantic capacity and robustness in complex environments. To address these challenges in radar signal modulation, this paper proposes a multimodal approach that combines image-text feature fusion with extreme value theory (EVT). This approach improves feature discrimination and enhances the model's ability to reject unknown classes. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method performs robustly across various signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels and unknown-class settings. Specifically, under challenging conditions where the number of unknown classes is 5 and the SNR is -6 dB, it achieves an acceptance rate of 95.56% and a rejection rate of 87.67%, highlighting its strong capability in handling unknown classes while maintaining competitive performance on known-class recognition.

title: Constrained Bayesian Optimisation with Multiple Information Sources
abstract: Bayesian Optimisation (BO) under unknown constraints is particularly challenging when feasible regions are small. In such settings, existing methods that typically rely solely on evaluations of the true objective and constraints struggle to efficiently explore the design space. However, many real-world applications offer auxiliary data sources (e.g. surrogate models or simplified simulations) that can support early exploration. Despite this potential, their integration into constrained BO remains largely unexplored. We propose a general multi-source framework that extends constrained Max-value Entropy Search, capturing inter-source correlation while balancing evaluation cost and information gain. Experiments on both synthetic and physics-based benchmarks show that our method efficiently identifies feasible and optimal solutions, even when auxiliary data are only weakly correlated. The proposed approach consistently outperforms existing methods, particularly in early-stage exploration.

title: LIST3R: Long-sequence Instance-aware 3D Reconstruction
abstract: We present LIST3R, an instance-aware framework for long-sequence 3D reconstruction inspired by the way humans organize spatial memory around stable and recognizable objects. LIST3R organizes long-sequence reconstruction around instance anchors, using them to reconnect fragmented subsequences and consolidate local observations into a coherent global 3D scene. Given a long video, our approach partitions it into overlapping subsequences and builds a structured local instance library for each partial reconstruction, maintaining persistent trackable anchors with semantic and geometric evidence. These anchors are matched across subsequences to recover revisited regions and provide object-aware constraints for fragment alignment, producing a consistent global reconstruction. During this process, the evolving geometric evidence updates the local instance libraries and progressively organizes them into a unified global 3D instance library. Experiments on long-sequence benchmarks show that our method produces more accurate trajectories and higher-quality 3D reconstructions, highlighting the effectiveness of persistent instance anchors for organizing long-horizon 3D reconstruction. Our code is available on the project page: https://yixn965.github.io/LIST3R/.

title: Formal Verification of Probing Security via Conditional Independence
abstract: Side-channel attacks are a major threat to the security of cryptosystems. Masking is a widely used countermeasure against such attacks, but proving the security of masked algorithms is error-prone without formal verification. In this work, we propose a novel approach to formal verification of noninterference properties of masked algorithms based on probabilistic separation logic. By establishing a connection between noninterference and conditional independence, we show how noninterference can be verified using Lilac, a separation logic for conditional independence. We also provide several proof rules that facilitate the verification of probing security and demonstrate their application to example algorithms.

title: Detección de anomalías de tráfico aéreo: un pipeline declarativo de etiquetado automático y aprendizaje supervisado
abstract: Los registros operacionales de tráfico aéreo constituyen una fuente relevante para el análisis, la planificación y la evaluación de la actividad aeronáutica. Los errores en atributos como la distancia entre aeropuertos, el tipo de aeronave, la ruta o los operadores pueden propagarse a los sistemas que utilizan estos datos. Su detección automática resulta especialmente compleja cuando no existe una verdad de referencia y un comportamiento infrecuente no implica necesariamente un error. Este trabajo abordó dicha problemática mediante el diseño de un procedimiento completo para generar señales de anomalía sobre datos no etiquetados y entrenar modelos capaces de reproducirlas. Se analizaron registros de vuelos IFR procedentes del sistema CFMU e integrados por CRIDA, con un volumen del orden de dos millones de operaciones. Como contribución principal, se desarrolló un pipeline declarativo de etiquetado automático en el que cada problema se define mediante una especificación ProblemSpec y se asigna, mediante un despachador común, a una de cinco familias de detectores: variables continuas unimodales, distribuciones multimodales, rareza de frecuencias, rutas habituales y reglas deterministas de dominio. Los umbrales se derivaron principalmente de la estructura empírica de los datos mediante estadísticos robustos, percentiles, modelos de mezclas gaussianas, el criterio BIC y el índice de Sarle. Las desviaciones se transformaron en puntuaciones continuas en [0, 1] mediante la función de Hill, se combinaron con la media geométrica y se acompañaron de factores de confianza y valores centinela para distinguir los vuelos normales de los no analizables. La implementación declarativa reprodujo los resultados de los procedimientos específicos previos con una diferencia inferior a 10−9 , lo que confirmó que la generalización arquitectónica preservó su comportamiento. Posteriormente, se entrenaron regresores independientes para la rareza del tipo de aeronave dentro de la flota del operador (score_AA) y para la desviación de la distancia respecto a las rutas habituales de cada combinación operador–aeronave (score_AAD). Los ensamblados de árboles representaron mejor que los modelos lineales regularizados las interacciones condicionales del dominio, y LightGBM se seleccionó como modelo de referencia para ambas puntuaciones. La evaluación por tramos mostró que las métricas globales podían ocultar la subestimación de las puntuaciones altas debido a la concentración extrema de observaciones próximas a cero. Se obtuvo un flujo reproducible, extensible y vectorizado que conecta la caracterización de anomalías, la generación de pseudoetiquetas y su aprendizaje mediante modelos predictivos. Los resultados no certifican anomalías reales frente a una referencia externa, pero proporcionan una base sistemática y auditable para priorizar registros potencialmente anómalos y orientar su validación posterior por expertos. --ABSTRACT-- Operational air traffic records constitute a relevant source of information for the analysis, planning, and assessment of aviation activity. Errors in attributes such as the distance between airports, aircraft type, route, or operators may propagate to the systems that rely on these data. Their automatic detection is particularly challenging when no ground truth is available and infrequent behaviour does not necessarily indicate an error. This work addressed this problem by designing a complete procedure for generating anomaly signals from unlabelled data and training models capable of reproducing them. IFR flight records from the CFMU system, integrated by CRIDA, were analysed, comprising approximately two million operations. As the main contribution, a declarative automatic labelling pipeline was developed in which each problem is defined through a ProblemSpec specification and assigned, by means of a common dispatcher, to one of five detector families: unimodal continuous variables, multimodal distributions, frequency rarity, usual routes, and deterministic domain rules. Thresholds were derived primarily from the empirical structure of the data using robust statistics, percentiles, Gaussian mixture models, the BIC criterion, and Sarle’s coefficient. Deviations were transformed into continuous scores in the range [0, 1] using the Hill function, combined through the geometric mean, and accompanied by confidence factors and sentinel values to distinguish normal flights from those that could not be analysed. The declarative implementation reproduced the results of the previous problem-specific procedures with a difference below 10−9 , confirming that the architectural generalisation preserved their behaviour. Independent regression models were subsequently trained to predict the rarity of an aircraft type within an operator’s fleet (score_AA) and the deviation of the distance from the usual routes associated with each operator–aircraft combination (score_AAD). Tree-based ensembles represented the conditional interactions of the domain more effectively than regularised linear models, and LightGBM was selected as the reference model for both scores. Evaluation across score ranges showed that global metrics could conceal the underestimation of high scores because of the extreme concentration of observations close to zero. A reproducible, extensible, and vectorised workflow was obtained, connecting anomaly characterisation, pseudo-label generation, and their learning through predictive models. The results do not certify the presence of actual anomalies against an external reference, but they provide a systematic and auditable basis for prioritising potentially anomalous records and guiding their subsequent validation by domain experts.

title: AI POWERED MULTI MODEL TEXT SUMMARIZATION AND EVALUATION SYSTEM WITH MULTILINGUAL SUPPORT
abstract: In today's digital landscape, vast streams of unstructured information are generated through research papers, news articles, websites, and legal records.Manually digesting this data requires prohibitive time and cognitive effort.To address this, we present an AI-Powered Multi-Model Text Summarization and Evaluation System with Multilingual Support, a scalable web application that rapidly extracts key semantic insights from extensive text repositories.The system ingests data via three dynamic inputs: direct plain text, document uploads (PDF/DOCX), and live web text scraped from user-provided URLs.To ensure comprehensive coverage, the framework concurrently executes six independent extractive algorithms Frequency-based, TF-IDF, TextRank, LexRank, LSA, and a hybrid Feature-Based flagship model.For automated accuracy verification, the system computes ROUGE benchmarks alongside semantic BERT scores.Finally, to bridge demographic barriers, a neural machine translation pipeline translates the summary outputs into regional Indian languages, specifically Telugu and Hindi, without losing factual alignment.

title: Intelligent Agents for Enterprise Knowledge Management Construction and Application Based on Large Language Models
abstract: This paper presents an intelligent agent for enterprise knowledge management, combining Large Language Models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and semantic embeddings to address challenges in unstructured communication data. The system integrates preprocessing, embedding generation, retrieval, summarization, question answering, and recommendations using the Enron Email Dataset. Evaluation results show high BERTScore (0.9275) for summarization with good semantic coherence despite low lexical similarity (low ROUGE scores). Retrieval performance includes Precision @k = 0.65, Recall @k = 0.9286, and nDCG@k = 0.9544, with strong contextual relevance. The model also demonstrates robust hallucination mitigation, with low hallucination rates (0.10) and high factual consistency. Scalability tests show a mean latency of 1.96 seconds and memory usage of 7.55 GB. Overall, the agent proves to be an effective solution for reducing information overload, enhancing decision-making, and preserving organizational memory.

title: The Impact of Organizational AI Adoption on Employee Adaptive Service Performance
abstract: Given that organizational artificial intelligence adoption fundamentally transforms employees’ work methods and job roles in the workplace, few studies have explored whether employees can adapt to this dynamic work environment. This study employs paradox theory to develop and test a conceptual model that explores the effect of organizational AI adoption on frontline employees’ adaptive service performance. Through an experimental design and a multi-wave time-lagged survey, the findings demonstrated that the impact of organizational AI adoption on paradox mindset and consequent adaptive service performance depends upon leader AI symbolization. Specifically, when leader AI symbolization is high, organizational AI adoption promotes adaptive service performance among frontline employees through a paradox mindset. This study highlights the importance of leadership in analyzing how organizational AI adoption affects employee adaptive outcomes, and also advancing our appreciation of the complicated impacts of AI adoption on adaptive service performance within dynamic environments.

title: SNAPKITTYWEST: Sovereign Compute Architecture with Linear Types, WORM Seals, Goldilocks Field Arithmetic, and Settlement Witnesses
abstract: SNAPKITTYWEST is an open-source sovereign computing framework that explores the intersection of systems programming, formal methods, cryptographic provenance, agent governance, and compiler design through a modular, local-first architecture. The current release comprises 18 interrelated software modules spanning linear type systems, compiler infrastructure, cryptographic addressing, finite-field arithmetic, distributed agent governance, esoteric programming language research, topological quantum computing experiments, port-Hamiltonian differential-algebraic equation modeling, and append-only WORM (Write Once, Read Many) artifact management. The architecture emphasizes deterministic execution, reproducibility, and verifiable software engineering through: Linear resource management implemented via a five-level type hierarchy (lin, aff, un, cap, seal) Cryptographically sealed artifact provenance using append-only SHA-256 WORM chains Deterministic canonical addressing through snapaddr:<64hex> content identifiers Goldilocks prime field arithmetic over p=264−232+1p = 2^{64} - 2^{32} + 1p=264−232+1 for finite-field computation Formal verification workflows integrating Lean 4 with deterministic compilation pipelines Policy-driven agent governance for auditable multi-agent execution Local-first infrastructure designed to minimize dependence on centralized cloud services This release expands the ecosystem with several new components, including: sovereign-addr — deterministic canonical content addressing (snapaddr:<64hex>) sovereign-prism — OCaml implementation of a typed ψ-pipeline for structural inference sovereign-pirtm — C++ compiler infrastructure for typed intermediate representations sovereign-agt — C# governance framework for agent identity, policy enforcement, and orchestration sovereign-multiplicity — deterministic execution and computational algebra modules sovereign-adr — architectural decision record framework root-fontana — constitutional compiler and symbolic governance layer Development is tracked through Git with cryptographically verifiable commit history beginning 2026-05-07, providing a reproducible record of architectural evolution and implementation. SNAPKITTYWEST is intended as a research platform for exploring trustworthy software systems, formal verification, compiler construction, deterministic AI infrastructure, and reproducible computational workflows. This release represents an active research software platform. Some modules are experimental, APIs may evolve, and several components remain under active development.

title: Impact of Intermediate Task Selection on Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance in XTREME
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the choice of intermediate task (e.g., natural language inference vs. question answering) affect the magnitude of performance gains in zero-shot cross-lingual transfer on XTREME when using multilingual vs. monolingual initialization? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.3/10.

title: The Static-Statistical Bridge: Connecting Epistemic Axiomatic Systems with Epiplexity (v6)
abstract: We establish a formal bridge between Epistemic Axiomatic Systems (EAS) and Epiplexity, a framework for quantifying cognitive quality in finite observers. We prove three theorems rigorously connecting these frameworks: (A) an information-theoretic lower bound on time-bounded entropy, (B) a categorical bridge functor that is faithful but not full, and (C) a three-way entropy decomposition separating unavoidable cardinality constraints from distribution mismatch, representation indexing cost, and computational overhead. Version 6 adds the discrete-continuous relationship narrative as a framework contribution: discrete-continuous are not two worlds requiring a bridge, but two observation modes of the same phenomenon.

title: Graph Diffusion SMOTE: Minority Sample Generation via Diffusion Propagation on Graphs
abstract: Class imbalance remains a critical challenge in graph-structured data learning, where majority classes heavily dominate the message-passing process of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), leading to severely sub-optimal performance on minority classes. Although conventional graph oversampling methods attempt to address this by interpolating new nodes within local feature spaces, they often neglect the global topological context and disrupt the structural consistency of the original network. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes Graph Diffusion SMOTE, a novel minority sample generation framework based on generalized graph diffusion propagation. The proposed method leverages a global graph diffusion matrix—specifically utilizing Personalized PageRank (PPR)—to accurately capture long-range topological dependencies and global context beyond the immediate first-order neighborhood. By mapping nodes into this diffusion space, the algorithm identifies high-quality topological neighbors for baseline minority nodes. Synthetic nodes are then generated via linear interpolation within the feature space, while their structural embeddings are consistently fused. Furthermore, a dynamic structure reconstruction mechanism based on a softmax probability distribution is introduced to establish rational edges between synthetic nodes and existing nodes via Bernoulli sampling. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that with sparsification techniques, the algorithm maintains favorable scalability for large-scale graphs. This global diffusion-driven approach ensures that the synthesized minority samples preserve both feature coherence and structural alignment, effectively mitigating the graph class imbalance problem.

title: A user-centric, ontology-driven and context-aware framework for real-time adaptive privacy protection and information retention within Multimodal AI Systems
abstract: This research proposes a norm-driven, user-centric and context-aware framework for privacy protection in real-time multimodal AI. Addressing the growing challenges of identity exposure in intelligent visual systems, the framework introduces an ontology-based model that integrates semantic reasoning, context-aware analysis, user-defined privacy protection settings and red lines to enable adaptive entity obfuscation. It integrates multiple recognition streams including face, object, scene, action, and emotion recognition, into a unified architecture that prioritises ethical alignment, regulatory compliance and individual requirements. A key methodological contribution is the introduction of two novel metrics: the Re-Identifiability Index (RII), which quantifies the privacy risk based on soft biometrics and scene context; and the Intelligibility Value Index (IVI), which measures the information utility retained after obfuscation. These indicators enable a dual-criteria privacy protection reasoning mechanism that dynamically adjusts masking based on both re-identification risk and interpretability value. In cases where a user chooses Auto Privacy or user authentication failures, an Auto Privacy mode is used to predict frame level privacy protection settings from multimodal features and historical behaviours that reduce the need for manual configuration. To ensure operation in real-time, the framework incorporates GPU acceleration, region-of-interest (ROI) processing and lightweight recognition models. A bespoke internal database maintains user profiles, entity class definitions and sensitivity categorisations. This integration enables real-time reasoning over recognised features, red-line policies and use-context metadata to ensure consistent and user-centric privacy protection. Experimental results, tested in smaller circles such as a university environment with groups of students and lecturers who know each other very well, demonstrated that the framework achieved 78.6% success rate in preventing re-identification, with 85.7% of users reporting satisfaction, 71.4% affirming that scene intelligibility was preserved at good levels and the remining 28.6% stating that it preserved at adequate levels. By combining ethical principles, norm-based decision-making and scalable ontology-driven reasoning, this research has advanced the state-of-the-art in privacy-preserving AI. It has delivered a scalable and normative context-aware privacy reasoning method for protecting identity in high privacy-risk, real world settings while maintaining alignment with GDPR principles and user expectations.

title: Chatbot con Inteligencia Artificial para la Gestión Proactiva de Permisos, Licencias y Riesgo Operacional
abstract: El estudio tuvo como objetivo desarrollar e implementar un chatbot con inteligencia artificial para optimizar la consulta y gestión de permisos del personal del área de talento humano de una institución pública, integrando validación normativa automática y clasificación proactiva de riesgo operativo. Se aplicó la metodología Agile/SCRUM sobre una arquitectura de microservicios. El componente conversacional se construyó con DeepPavlov, complementado por Google Gemini en un rol acotado de enriquecimiento y contingencia; un motor de reglas en Python validó el cumplimiento normativo y un clasificador con scikit-learn estimó el riesgo operativo. La validación se realizó mediante seis casos de prueba funcionales. Los resultados evidenciaron la integración de las cuatro capacidades del chatbot, la clasificación correcta de los tres niveles de riesgo y la continuidad operativa ante fallos de servicios externos. Se concluyó que el enfoque híbrido demostró ser viable para la automatización proactiva de permisos en el sector público, ofreciendo trazabilidad institucional y respuestas adaptativas.

title: Suspending Judgement: Belief Contraction in Dynamic Epistemic Logic
abstract: We look at multi-agent versions of three different belief contraction operations (severe withdrawal, conservative contraction and moderate contraction), considering them as dynamic operations on plausibility models, meant to represent joint actions of “suspension of belief” by groups of agents (or by individual agents). We provide sound and complete axiomatizations, in the presence of standard static operators such as conditional belief, knowledge and safe belief.

title: DEEP LEARNING FOR FINANCIAL ANALYTICS: NETWORK REPRESENTATION LEARNING AND AI ALIGNMENT
abstract: This dissertation develops deep learning approaches for Fintech applications, with a focus on learning and aligning representations from unstructured financial data to support high-stakes decision-making. It addresses key problems including peer firm identification, credit risk prediction, and the adaptation of large language models (LLMs) for financial contexts. By integrating large-scale unstructured data from social media, multiplex corporate networks, and earnings calls, the studies introduce novel approaches that capture firm relationships and generate financially meaningful insights with improved accuracy and interpretability. The first chapter introduces a data-driven approach to identify peer firms using a firm-firm network based on co-mentions in social media posts. Unlike traditional methods that rely on static industry classifications, we utilize network representation learning to capture latent firm-firm structures, where peers are then identified through firm embeddings. The method outperforms existing techniques in explaining cross-sectional variations in monthly returns and financial metrics. We also conduct interpretability analyses to reveal the encoded financial ratios in the learned embeddings and the firm similarities as a pair-trading strategy for positive alpha. The second chapter extends network representation learning to a heterogeneous context with multiple node and edge types. We develop a multiplex network approach that incorporate firms’ supply chain (SC), director, and analyst relations, augmenting traditional financial ratios with relational dynamics. The attention mechanism highlights the relative importance of entities (SC partners, SC customers, directors, or analysts) in driving predictions, while motif-based GNNs capture high-order network structures, providing interpretable explanations for their impact on credit ratings. The third chapter focuses on LLM alignment to generate analyst-style reports that demonstrate finance-specific reasoning capabilities. We introduce domain-specific evaluation metrics capturing sentiment, language style, and content coverage, and show that baseline LLMs fail to reflect critical domain nuances. To address this, we propose a multi-objective alignment approach that incorporates linguistic signals, significantly improving report alignment to human language. The aligned models achieve predictive performance comparable to human analysts and provide incremental value for explaining and forecasting market reactions.

title: Hybrid Large Language Model-Reinforcement Learning Pipeline to Enhance Simulation Training for Robotics
abstract: Despite rapid advances in artificial intelligence, robotic systems remain limited by poor generalisation across unstructured environments and fragile training pipelines. Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise in training robotics, yet its effectiveness is often constrained by manually engineered reward mechanisms. In parallel, large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong reasoning and evaluation capabilities that remain underutilised in robotic training pipelines. This paper proposes a hybrid LLM-RL framework in which an LLM dynamically evaluates robot performance during simulation training and adaptively modifies the reward weights to improve learning stability, accuracy of task completion, and policy convergence. Unlike existing work that focuses on natural language control at inference time, the proposed method leverages the LLM during training, acting as a high-level reward critic. We implemented this framework using an open-source robotic arm trained in simulation to demonstrate improved task success rates and learning efficiency compared to static reward mechanisms. This work highlights a scalable pathway toward more adaptive and generalisable robotic training systems for advanced robotics.

title: Bernoulli filter based joint sensor bias compensation and target tracking
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of joint target tracking and sensor bias compensation in multi-sensor tracking systems, where spatial biases stem from factors such as inaccurate sensor calibration or platform positioning uncertainty, coexisting with observation noise. While augmented state filtering offers a direct framework for addressing this issue, the accuracy of bias estimation critically depends on correct data association. In cluttered environments with missed detections, erroneous data associations can significantly corrupt state estimates, resulting in performance degradation or even filter divergence. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a novel approach termed the Augmented State Unscented Gaussian Mixture Bernoulli Filter (AS-UGM-BF). This method integrates unknown sensor biases into an augmented state vector, combining them with the target's kinematic state to form a high-dimensional estimation problem. The posterior probability density of this augmented state is then recursively propagated within the Bernoulli filter framework. This framework naturally handles observation uncertainties in a probabilistic manner, thereby providing a robust foundation for the joint estimation of the augmented state. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed AS-UGM-BF.

title: QCOEM: Quantum Cloud Orchestration with Evolutionary Multi-Objective Optimization
abstract: Quantum cloud platforms need to dynamically orchestrate workloads across heterogeneous quantum computation backends whose noise profiles, qubit topologies, and queues vary over time. Existing orchestrators use noise-agnostic heuristics that ignore backend-specific errors, causing reduced execution fidelity, load imbalance, and frequent rescheduling. To address these challenges, we propose QCOEM - a Quantum Cloud Orchestration framework that leverages Evolutionary algorithms for Multi-objective optimization of quantum task scheduling. We compare NSGA-II and NSGA-III for jointly minimizing mean completion time, execution error rate, and load imbalance. To select schedules from a non-convex Pareto front, we apply an Augmented Achievement Scalarization Function (AASF) as a preference-based decision rule that maps the Pareto set to a single dispatchable schedule aligned with user priorities. Our extensive performance evaluation in a heterogeneous quantum cloud environment shows zero task rescheduling and about 30% higher mean fidelity than noise-agnostic heuristics, while maintaining bounded scheduling overhead. The experiment results indicate that our QCOEM framework can deliver stable, high-fidelity execution and lightweight resource management for quantum cloud computing.

title: An automated method of identifying incorrectly labelled images based on the sequences of loss functions of deep learning networks
abstract: Deep learning is widely applied in medical image analysis, but up to 10% of manually labelled images may be incorrect, degrading model performance. This paper proposes an automated method to identify incorrectly labelled medical images by analyzing sequences of loss functions from deep learning classification networks over multiple training epochs. Identified images can be reviewed and relabelled by experts, improving dataset quality and model performance. Two experiments validate the method on a fundus image dataset for referable diabetic retinopathy screening. In the first, 6% (648) of 10,788 gold-standard labels were intentionally flipped. The method identified 75.31% (488) of the flipped samples, with only 4.85% (492) false positives among correctly labelled samples. In the second, reviewing and correcting the 980 identified samples (9.1% of the dataset) and retraining the model improved best accuracy on an independent test set from 95.93% (with 6% label noise) to 96.50% (with 1.5% noise), approaching the ideal 96.57% (with 0% noise). The results demonstrate the method's effectiveness in improving model performance through automated label quality control.

title: Learning to Compose: Revisiting Proxy Task Design for Zero-Shot Composed Image Retrieval
abstract: Composed Image Retrieval (CIR) retrieves a target image from a reference image and a textual modification. While supervised CIR relies on costly triplets, Zero-Shot CIR (ZS-CIR) alleviates this reliance through proxy tasks trained on image-text pairs. However, existing proxy tasks primarily enhance visual and textual representations to accommodate a predefined composition mechanism such as pseudo-word injection into a frozen text encoder or linear feature arithmetic. As a result, the composition function itself remains unlearned, limiting the model's ability to express diverse and fine-grained semantic modifications. To address this, we propose FoCo, which models composition as two coordinated stages: focusing on modification-relevant visual content, and then completing the target semantics. We realize these through two proxy tasks: text-anchored visual aggregation to selectively gather visual content guided by localized textual semantics, and context-conditioned semantic completion to transform these aggregated visuals with the remaining scene context into a coherent composed representation. The tasks are trained jointly with a cross-instance contrastive objective, encouraging semantic diversity and discouraging shortcut composition strategies. Extensive experiments on four ZS-CIR benchmarks show FoCo's state-of-the-art performance and improved generalization.

title: Evaluación comparativa de arquitecturas encoder y grandes modelos de lenguaje para el reconocimiento de entidades clínicas en español
abstract: El Reconocimiento de Entidades Nombradas (NER) es una tarea del Procesamiento del Lenguaje Natural que consiste en localizar y clasificar términos dentro de textos no estructurados. En el ámbito biomédico, su aplicación permite la extracción automatizada de información clínica; sin embargo, la complejidad inherente al lenguaje médico plantea retos significativos. Históricamente, este campo ha estado dominado por modelos basados en el componente codificador de la arquitectura Transformer, como RoBERTa. No obstante, la creciente adopción de Grandes Modelos de Lenguaje (LLMs) generativos, basados en el componente decodificador de dicha arquitectura, hace necesario comparar ambos enfoques en términos de precisión y eficiencia. Este Trabajo Fin de Máster evalúa esta cuestión en el dominio clínico en español utilizando los corpus DisTEMIST (enfermedades) y ProcTEMIST (procedimientos), basados en 1.000 casos reales. Se comparan cinco codificadores entrenados con técnicas supervisadas frente a seis LLMs de código abierto y GPT-4.1-mini, modelo propietario de OpenAI. Estos modelos se evalúan tanto en estrategias sin ajuste de parámetros, incluyendo aprendizaje en contexto con y sin ejemplos (in-context learning), como en ajuste fino supervisado con técnicas eficientes como QLoRA. Para garantizar la comparabilidad con las competiciones originales, se aplica la misma métrica empleada en dichas shared tasks, que exige identificar la posición exacta de cada término en el texto. Los resultados muestran que los codificadores obtienen los mejores resultados, con un F1 estricto de 0,805 en ProcTEMIST y 0,797 en DisTEMIST. El mejor modelo abierto, Ministral-3-8B-Instruct, obtiene resultados similares tras el entrenamiento con QLoRA (0,793 en ambos corpus), próximos a los del modelo comercial GPT-4.1-mini (0,803 y 0,795). En el análisis cualitativo, los codificadores tienden a recortar entidades largas, mientras que los LLMs amplían los límites y presentan mayor frecuencia de alucinaciones. Asimismo, los codificadores procesan documentos en menos de 0,22 segundos, con una velocidad de inferencia entre 60× y 100× superior a la de los modelos generativos. En conclusión, los codificadores constituyen la opción más adecuada cuando se dispone de datos de entrenamiento, dada su velocidad y precisión. Los modelos generativos representan una alternativa en escenarios con escasez de datos, al extraer una proporción considerable de entidades sin requerir entrenamiento previo. --ABSTRACT-- Named Entity Recognition (NER) is a Natural Language Processing task that locates and classifies concepts within unstructured texts. Its application in the biomedical domain supports the automated extraction of clinical information, although the complexity of medical language introduces challenges. Historically, this field has been dominated by models based on the encoder component of the Transformer architecture, such as RoBERTa. The increasing adoption of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), based on the decoder component of that architecture, makes it necessary to compare both approaches in terms of performance and efficiency. This Master’s Thesis evaluates this question within the Spanish clinical domain using the DisTEMIST (diseases) and ProcTEMIST (procedures) corpora, built upon 1,000 real cases. Five encoders trained with supervised techniques are evaluated against six open-source LLMs and GPT-4.1-mini, a proprietary model from OpenAI. These models are assessed under both parameter-free strategies, including in-context learning with and without examples, and supervised fine-tuning with efficient techniques such as QLoRA. To ensure comparability with the original competitions, the same strict metric used in those shared tasks is applied, requiring the exact character-level position of each term to be identified. Results show that encoders achieve the highest performance, with a strict F1 of 0.805 on ProcTEMIST and 0.797 on DisTEMIST. The best open-source model, Ministral-3-8BInstruct, obtains similar results after QLoRA training (0.793 on both corpora), close to those of the commercial model GPT-4.1-mini (0.803 and 0.795). In the qualitative analysis, encoders tend to truncate long entities, whereas LLMs expand boundaries and show a higher frequency of hallucinations. Furthermore, encoders process documents in under 0.22 seconds, with inference speeds between 60× and 100× higher than generative models. In conclusion, encoders represent the most suitable option when training data is available, given their speed and precision. Generative models constitute an alternative in low-data scenarios, extracting a considerable proportion of entities without requiring prior training.

title: TEXT MINING SENTIMEN MAHASISWA KAPUTAMA MENGENAI FASILITAS JARINGAN WI-FI KAMPUS MENGGUNAKAN METODE SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE (SVM)
abstract: ABSTRAK Perkembangan teknologi informasi di perguruan tinggi memerlukan fasilitas Wi-Fi yang mendukung aktivitas akademik mahasiswa. Namun, kualitas layanan Wi-Fi yang kurang optimal sering menimbulkan keluhan, sehingga diperlukan analisis sentimen untuk memahami persepsi mahasiswa. Penelitian ini menggunakan teknik text mining dengan metode Support Vector Machine (SVM) untuk mengklasifikasikan sentimen terhadap fasilitas Wi-Fi di STMIK Kaputama Binjai. Data penelitian berupa 500 ulasan mahasiswa yang diperoleh melalui kuesioner pada Januari 2026. Pengolahan data meliputi case folding, cleaning, tokenizing, stopword removal, normalisasi, stemming, pembobotan TF-IDF, dan klasifikasi SVM. Hasil menunjukkan sentimen negatif mendominasi (52,6%), diikuti positif (35,6%) dan netral (11,8%). Model mencapai akurasi 81,33%, menunjukkan bahwa SVM efektif untuk analisis sentimen dan evaluasi kualitas layanan Wi-Fi kampus. Penelitian ini juga menghasilkan visualisasi distribusi sentimen untuk pihak kampus dan peneliti. Kata Kunci: Analisis Sentimen, Support Vector Machine, Text Mining, WiFi Kampus

title: How GenZ perceive AI driven advertisement
abstract: The fast development of artificial intelligence (AI) has greatly changed the advertising industry since it allows making marketing messages personalized, automated, and Data-driven. This paper looks at the perception of AI generated adverts by Generation Z based on aspects like previous exposure, customization, credibility, and ethical issues. The data were collected with the help of a quantitative research design in a form of a structured questionnaire, which included 150 Gen Z respondents, and analyzed with the help of the Python-based statistical applications, such as correlation and multiple regression. The results show that personalization and trust positively and significantly affect perceptions of AI-generated advertisement, whereas prior exposure and ethical considerations do not have a statistically significant effect. The paper highlights the value of transparency, trust-building, and responsible AI use in properly engaging Gen Z consumers and offers guidance to marketers that aim to use AI-based advertising methodologically

title: When Coaching Doesn't Cash Out: Identity Salience and the Social Gate on AI-Taught Skills
abstract: Large language models enable friction free coaching at scale, but a core question remains under answered: when do AI taught skills survive the jump from practice to real performance, and for whom? We examine an LLM driven negotiation tutor that delivers diagnostic feedback by identifying dialogue level negotiation errors with at least 90% accuracy. Across two studies, we uncover a sharp discontinuity between learning and payoff. In a practice context designed to minimize identity cueing, diagnostic feedback disproportionately improves performance for East Asian and White women, narrowing gaps. However, introducing a single identity cue, telling participants that their counterpart is a White man, changes the conversion of learning into economic returns. Learning persists as errors decline, yet outcome gains fragment along gender by ethnicity lines. These findings demonstrate that AI coaching can teach enacted skills, but whether those skills pay off depends on social context and identity salience. We conclude by outlining an identity savvy design agenda for AI coaching as socio technical infrastructure for equitable talent development.

title: p-kit
abstract: p-kit is a Python library for simulating probabilistic circuits using p-bits that fluctuate between -1 and +1. It implements two frameworks: PSL (Probabilistic Spin Logic) for invertible classical logic via Gibbs sampling, and PAOA (Probabilistic Approximate Optimization Algorithms) as a probabilistic analog of QAOA for combinatorial optimization.

title: Research on an Improved SMOTE Algorithm Based on Data Distribution Shaping Mechanism
abstract: Class imbalance is a persistent and critical challenge in the fields of machine learning and data mining. Although the traditional Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates this issue by interpolating new samples between minority instances, its localized "point-to-point" generation approach frequently overlooks the macro-topological structure of the data. This limitation often results in manifold fracture, severe class overlap, and suboptimal generalization performance. To address these deficiencies, this paper proposes an innovative over-sampling approach termed Data-shaping SMOTE. Moving beyond the conventional perspective of generating isolated data points, the proposed algorithm focuses on reshaping the entire underlying distribution geometry of the minority class. By introducing a framework based on manifold reconstruction and energy functional minimization, Data-shaping SMOTE coordinates global covariance adjustments, localized kernel density smoothing, and topological preservation constraints. This holistic transformation allows the synthetic minority instances to form a smooth, continuous, and physically coherent manifold shape, effectively sharpening the classification boundaries. Theoretical analysis indicates that the proposed algorithm significantly mitigates over-fitting and enhances boundary definition. Consequently, it yields substantial improvements in classification robustness across complex, high-dimensional imbalanced datasets, as demonstrated by enhanced F1-Score, G-Mean, and AUC performance.

By introducing a framework based on manifold reconstruction and energy functional minimization, Data-shaping SMOTE coordinates global covariance adjustments, localized kernel density smoothing, and topological preservation constraints. This holistic transformation allows the synthetic minority instances to form a smooth, continuous, and physically coherent manifold shape, effectively sharpening the classification boundaries. Theoretical analysis indicates that the proposed algorithm significantly mitigates over-fitting and enhances boundary definition. Consequently, it yields substantial improvements in classification robustness across complex, high-dimensional imbalanced datasets, as demonstrated by enhanced F1-Score, G-Mean, and AUC performance.

title: Exploring deep reinforcement learning acceleration by superscaling data augmentation via branched fractal symmetries
abstract: Learning deep reinforcement learning (DRL) policies directly in physical robots remains bottlenecked by slow wall-clock training times. We present preliminary research on Branched Euclidean Group Fractal Symmetries , a trajectory-level augmentation framework that super-scales group transformations to accelerate policy learning for manipulation. We model a Markov decision process (MDP) as a tree of state–action pairs; at each depth, affine transformations generate geometric structures, within which combinations of Euclidean group symmetries produce a large set of unique symmetric equivalences. A self-similar branching rule can also be iterated across depths to yield fractal symmetry expansions that populate the replay buffer with diverse yet consistent experiences with Cartesian or hand-centered image representations. We show the efficacy of our approach through simulated and real Franka robot manipulation contact tasks. Our study learns robust policies directly in physical robots in as fast as 14 min and in 20 min of wall-clock time on average. The code is accessible at https://github.com/lippyRobotics/fractalserl .

title: Analisis Komparatif Model Machine Learning Berbasis Boosting dalam Analisis Sentimen Ulasan Pengguna Neobank di Google Play Store
abstract: Perkembangan layanan perbankan digital terutama pada aplikasi neobank di Indonesia mendorong meningkatnya jumlah ulasan pengguna di platform Google Play Store, sehingga dibutuhkan metode yang efektif untuk menganalisis opini tersebut secara otomatis. Ulasan pengguna menjadi sumber penting untuk memahami kepuasan dan keluhan nasabah. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk membandingkan performa algoritma machine learning berbasis boosting, yaitu XGBoost, LightGBM, dan CatBoost, dalam klasifikasi sentimen ulasan pengguna aplikasi Neobank. Data sebanyak 6.963 ulasan dikumpulkan melalui teknik web scraping pada periode Oktober 2025 hingga Februari 2026. Data tersebut kemudian diproses melalui tahapan text preprocessing yang meliputi case folding, pembersihan karakter, tokenisasi, penghapusan stopword, dan stemming menggunakan Sastrawi. Pelabelan sentimen dilakukan secara otomatis dengan pendekatan berbasis leksikon menggunakan kamus InSet (Indonesia Sentiment Lexicon) ke dalam kelas positif dan negatif. Pembobotan kata menggunakan TF-IDF dengan kombinasi unigram dan bigram. Untuk mengatasi ketidakseimbangan kelas, diterapkan teknik SMOTE hanya pada data latih di setiap fold. Evaluasi model dilakukan menggunakan 5-Fold Cross Validation dengan pembagian data 80:20. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa XGBoost mencapai performa terbaik dengan akurasi rata-rata sebesar 94,30%, presisi 94,35%, recall 94,51%, dan F1-Score 94,37%, diikuti CatBoost dengan akurasi 91,25% dan LightGBM dengan akurasi 91,16%. Seluruh model ini menunjukkan performa di atas 90%, menandakan efektivitas pendekatan yang digunakan. Keunggulan XGBoost diduga karena kemampuannya menangani data sparse dari TF-IDF serta regularisasi yang baik. Ketiga algoritma terbukti mampu mengklasifikasikan sentimen ulasan pengguna Neobank secara akurat, dengan XGBoost sebagai model yang paling unggul dalam pengujian ini.

title: Towards Accurate Yet Efficient Federated Learning as a Service Via Personalized Lora Rank Allocation
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables multiple clients to collaboratively train a shared model without exchanging raw data, making it an important paradigm for privacy-preserving distributed intelligence. Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique, significantly reduces communication and computation costs by updating low-rank adapters instead of full model parameters, and has therefore been increasingly adopted in FL systems. As FL evolves toward Federated Learning as a Service (FLaaS), scalable and automated management of LoRA capacity across heterogeneous clients becomes a key challenge for practical service deployment. However, most existing LoRA-based FL approaches assign a fixed rank to all participants and therefore perform inefficiently under heterogeneous data distributions. Alternatively, several methods attempt to personalize ranks through iterative multi-round adjustments, which introduce additional communication and computational overhead that is undesirable in service-oriented environments. To address this issue, we propose OneLoRA, an automated rank allocation method tailored for FLaaS platforms. OneLoRA leverages the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to the Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) to evaluate client-level data complexity and perform one-shot personalized LoRA rank assignment before training begins. By enabling capacity-aware rank allocation without iterative tuning, OneLoRA avoids additional communication rounds and maintains the lightweight characteristics required for service-oriented FL systems. Experiments show that the client ranks automatically allocated by OneLoRA slightly outperform the manually tuned RBLA baseline. Compared with state-of-theart methods, OneLoRA improves accuracy by up to 27.27% and speeds up model convergence by up to 37.85%, while reducing communication and computational overhead by up to 35.11%.

title: Lightweight Cryptanalysis in Resource-Constrained Environments: A Systematic Review
abstract: Cryptanalysis plays a vital role in evaluating al-gorithmic robustness and ensuring resilience against emerging threats. This paper provides a comprehensive examination of lightweight cryptanalysis, incorporating the latest developments in the field. It offers an in-depth survey of techniques targeting lightweight ciphers designed for platforms with limited computational capacity, including Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems. The study encompasses both theoretical and practical dimensions. It analyses attack strategies such as differential, linear, and side-channel methods, identifies gaps in physical-leakage research, and reviews countermeasures intended to mitigate associated risks. By synthesising current research and recent findings, this work aims to inform future efforts to strengthen lightweight cryptographic primitives for secure IoT deployments.

title: High-gain effects in broadband continuous-wave parametric down conversion sources and measurements with undetected photons
abstract: Abstract We study theoretically how high-gain effects affect the measurement outcome of visible signal spectra in undetected photon measurement schemes. We consider two interferometric configurations: firstly, the SU(1,1) interferometer where the idler incurs loss and additional dispersion in between two identical, lossless, squeezers; secondly, the induced coherence interferometer where the idler incurs loss and additional dispersion in between two identical, lossless, squeezers and where the second squeezer is seeded by the idler and a vacuum ancilla mode. Furthermore, we consider a distributed loss configuration where the idler incurs loss as it propagates in the nonlinear medium. Motivated by experimental evidence and due to the fact that broadband sources are ideal for these measurement schemes, we use the dispersive data of a third-order dispersion engineered integrated waveguide parametric down conversion (PDC) source presented in Roeder et al (2024 New J. Phys. 26 123025) to model the PDC spectra in the three configurations. For each configuration we consider the case of idler-only (i) absorption, (ii) additional dispersion, and (iii) the combined effects. We obtain results which outline the strength and weaknesses of the different configurations at different operation points.

title: An LLM Framework for Regional Climate Services: Integrating Climate Knowledge and Ensemble Projections
abstract: Abstract Recent advances in generative AI have enabled the integration of scientific knowledge into natural language interfaces. However, existing large language models (LLMs) lack domain‐specific expertise and cannot directly utilize simulation data essential for risk assessment. This study develops a climatology‐specific LLM fine‐tuned on climate science literature and augmented with ensemble projection data set, aiming to support local governments and small enterprises in climate adaptation planning as a preliminary support tool. The framework combines domain‐specific fine‐tuning, retrieval‐augmented generation (RAG) for scientific documents and local guidelines, and future projection data. The developed model demonstrated highly competitive performance compared to general‐purpose LLMs such as Swallow 70B on climate‐specific benchmarks in both English and Japanese, particularly in the categories of “Impacts, adaptation, and vulnerability” and “Mitigation.” A case study in Kumagaya City, Japan, demonstrated that the model can quantitatively update heat‐mitigation measures using probabilistic projections and dynamically retrieved local constraints, generating data‐informed baselines to facilitate human deliberation under multiple warming scenarios. The proposed approach bridges the gap between climate science and the early stages of adaptation planning by enabling AI‐driven access to both textual and numerical climate knowledge. By lowering technical barriers to expert‐level analysis, it facilitates inclusive and data‐driven climate services for diverse stakeholders. This study represents the first systematic demonstration of an LLM that integrates ensemble projection data to support regionally grounded adaptation planning, contributing to the development of next‐generation climate services that enhance local resilience.

title: Performance analysis of the homomorphic implementation of K-Means using CKKS
abstract: Abstract Modern data science requires large amounts of data and computational power to perform effectively. However, there is a lot of sensitive data that should not be shared with others. To still do data science, methods like Homomorphic Encryption exist that enable calculations on encrypted data. One well-known data science algorithm is K-Means, which clusters data points into a previously fixed number of clusters. We provided a homomorphic implementation by demonstrating how comparisons and assignments of clusters can be calculated. Furthermore, the algorithm is evaluated in an offline approach with bootstrapping and an online approach with client re-encryption. Both achieve an accuracy of 100%, but take significantly longer, ranging from 50,000 to 16 million times compared to the non-encrypted case.

title: Deep Linear Discriminant Analysis Revisited
abstract: Abstract We show that for unconstrained Deep Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) classifiers, maximum-likelihood training admits pathological solutions in which class means drift together, covariances collapse, and the learned representation becomes almost non-discriminative. Conversely, cross-entropy training yields excellent accuracy but decouples the head from the underlying generative model, leading to highly inconsistent parameter estimates. To reconcile generative structure with discriminative performance, we introduce the Discriminative Negative Log-Likelihood (DNLL) loss, which augments the LDA log-likelihood with a simple penalty on the mixture density. DNLL can be interpreted as standard LDA NLL plus a term that explicitly discourages regions where several classes are simultaneously likely. Deep LDA trained with DNLL produces clean, well-separated latent spaces, matches the test accuracy of softmax classifiers on synthetic data and standard image benchmarks, and yields substantially better calibrated predictive probabilities.

title: Efficient private PEZ protocols without binary-input restrictions
abstract: Abstract Balogh et al. proposed deterministic secure multiparty computation called private PEZ protocols . In their work, a general construction of private PEZ protocols for computing an arbitrary function with n inputs is presented, but the function’s inputs must be binary . Binary domains are sufficient for computing functions with arbitrary domains because we can use the binary expansion of the inputs. However, such an expansion makes the protocol inefficient because unnecessary privacy is considered among the expanded bits of each input. Hence, we remove the binary expansion technique in this paper and propose a new private PEZ protocol directly applicable to functions with arbitrary domains. The proposed private PEZ protocol for an arbitrary function is much more efficient than Balogh et al.’s protocol. Concretely, an efficiency measure called the length of an initial string is exponentially improved in the domain size m : the order obtained from our construction is $$\mathcal {O}((2m)^{m^{n-1}})$$ O ( ( 2 m ) m n - 1 ) , while the construction of Balogh et al. yields $$\mathrm {\Omega }\bigg (\bigg (2^{\frac{m}{2}}\bigg )^{m^{n-1}}\bigg )$$ Ω ( ( 2 m 2 ) m n - 1 ) . The key idea of our protocol is called the divide and cue strategy, based on a recursive structure of views in private PEZ protocols.

title: Sign in the Air to Unlock: An Interface for authentication in Virtual and Augmented Reality Powered by Point-Voxel Cross-Attention Network
abstract: Significant advancement of immersive technologies such as Virtual and Augmented Reality (VR/AR) and their integration into diverse aspects of modern life need authentication interfaces that are secure, intuitive, and compatible with embodied interaction. Traditional methods such as passwords, PINs, and device-based logins, break immersion and rely on external hardware. Recent 3D-specific behavioral approaches, such as hand-gesture, eye-tracking, and electroencephalography (EEG)-based methods, offer promising alternatives but often require specialized sensors or constrain natural movement, limiting usability in dynamic environments. We present Sign in the Air to Unlock, an in-air signature interface that enables users to authenticate by signing naturally in 3D space which is a familiar, personal, and reproducible gesture. To realize this interface, we design a point-voxel Cross-Attention Network (PV-Net) that jointly models local motion dynamics and global spatial structure from 3D trajectories. title: When Context Compensates for Sparse Event History: AlphaEarth for Spatio-Temporal Point-Process Forecasting
abstract: Spatio-temporal point-process models must often generalise across space when local event histories are sparse. We study whether exogenous spatial context can compensate in such regimes. Using a fixed log-Gaussian Cox process backbone, we compare an event-only model with the same model augmented by AlphaEarth embeddings as linear spatial context. We evaluate spatial transfer on emergency medical services (EMS) forecasting across eight held-out regions, fixed forecast anchors, and a sweep over history length $w$, using only AlphaEarth (AE) embeddings available strictly before each anchor. AE improves out-of-region predictive performance across all history regimes, with the largest gains under scarce histories: approximately $2$--$6\times$ multiplicative improvements at $1-2$ weeks, tapering to roughly $10$--$20\%$ at $w=20$--$104$ weeks. These results show that contextual information can substantially stabilise spatially transferred point-process forecasts when event history is limited.

title: Semantic-Guided Reading Order Reconstruction in Historical Armenian Newspapers with LLMs
abstract: This paper addresses reading order reconstruction in historical Armenian newspapers, which combine complex layouts with limited language resources. We introduce a new annotated dataset of 66 pages and compare geometric heuristics, YOLO-based layout parsing, an end-to-end document model ECLAIR, and a hybrid method combining semantic zone detection with a generative LLM. Our hybrid method achieves the lowest error rates of all evaluated approaches, reducing ordering errors by up to 76% over the strongest geometric baseline, and remains robust in multi-page settings and under noisy OCR. Rather than targeting production the method is designed as a data bootstrapping strategy enabling rapid annotation in highly under-resourced scenarios. Alongside the dataset, we release a specialized Tesseract OCR model for historical Armenian print.

title: Quantum Simulation of Stokes Flow via Schrödingerisation and Artificial Compressibility
abstract: Simulating incompressible Stokes flow is essential for studies in microfluidics and low-Reynolds number hydrodynamics. However, the computational cost of resolving the associated saddle-point problem grows prohibitively with the dimensionality of the problem. In this work, we present a quantum algorithm based on the Schrödingerisation technique for the Stokes equations, incorporating an artificial compressibility regularization. The core of our approach is the design of an explicit quantum circuit that encodes the resulting regularized system. The artificial compressibility formulation provides a unified framework for the system, which is then efficiently mapped to a quantum circuit via the Schrödingerisation procedure. A rigorous complexity analysis demonstrates the quantum computational advantage of our algorithms in high-dimensional settings, notably an exponential speedup in problem dimensionality. The validity and scalability of the proposed method are corroborated by numerical simulations performed on Qiskit.

title: Spanish DBpedia: update pipeline audit and large-scale NLP resource construction from Wikipedia
abstract: Este Trabajo Fin de Máster aborda la fiabilidad y completitud del conjunto de datos de DBpedia en español (esDBpedia) mediante el análisis de su proceso de actualización automática, responsable de recuperar periódicamente datos desde DBpedia Databus. Las observaciones preliminares sugerían que la actualización no estaba funcionando correctamente, lo que podría provocar la existencia de datos desactualizados o incompletos. Sin embargo, una inspección detallada del flujo de actualización reveló que la resolución de este problema queda fuera del alcance de este trabajo. La causa principal se encuentra en el propio proceso de extracción de DBpedia, ya que la plataforma Databus no está publicando actualmente nuevos datos. Dado que el proceso de actualización automática permanece suspendido, este estudio reorienta sus esfuerzos hacia la creación de nuevos conjuntos de datos que constituyan recursos valiosos para diversas tareas de inteligencia artificial. Con este objetivo, se construye un corpus de gran escala y alta calidad en español compuesto por aproximadamente dos millones de artículos de la Wikipedia. Para maximizar su utilidad, este corpus principal se ofrece en distintas variantes, incluyendo versiones que conservan elementos complejos, como tablas y ecuaciones matemáticas, y versiones en las que dichos elementos han sido eliminados. Además de la publicación de este corpus principal, también se proporcionan nuevos conjuntos de datos derivados del mismo. Específicamente, los conjuntos de sinónimos (que pueden apoyar directamente tareas como la expansión de consultas y la sustitución léxica) se derivan de la estructura de redirecciones de los volcados de datos, dado que las redirecciones codifican inherentemente la equivalencia entre términos. Los candidatos a neologismos, útiles para rastrear la evolución léxica en recursos de PLN en español, también se proporcionan como una colección separada. Complementando estos, se publica igualmente un conjunto de datos de frecuencias de tokens, que ofrece un recurso ligero pero informativo para el análisis de vocabulario y las estadísticas de corpus. --ABSTRACT-- This Master’s Thesis addresses the reliability and completeness of the Spanish DBpedia (esDBpedia) dataset by analyzing its automatic update process, which is responsible for periodically retrieving data from the DBpedia Databus. Preliminary observations suggested that the current pipeline was not functioning correctly, potentially leading to outdated or missing data. However, a detailed inspection of the update workflow revealed that resolving this pipeline failure lies beyond the scope of this work. The root problem originates from the upstream DBpedia extraction process itself, as the Databus platform is currently not publishing new data. While the automated update process remains suspended, this study pivots to the creation of new datasets that serve as valuable resources for various downstream artificial intelligence tasks in the meantime. To this end, a large-scale, high-quality Spanish corpus comprising approximately 2 million articles from Wikipedia is constructed. To maximize its utility, this main corpus is provided in different variants, including versions that conserve complex elements such as tables and mathematical equations and versions that omit them. In addition to publishing this main corpus, newly generated datasets derived from it are also released. Specifically, synonym sets (which can directly support tasks such as query expansion and lexical substitution) are derived from the redirect structure of the data dumps, given that redirects inherently encode equivalence between terms. Neologism candidates, useful for tracking lexical evolution in Spanish NLP resources, are also provided as a separate collection. Complementing these, a token frequency dataset is also released, offering a lightweight but informative resource for vocabulary analysis and corpus statistics.

title: Design and analysis of periodically deniable ring signature scheme based on HQC
abstract: To address the limitation that existing periodically deniable ring signature schemes rely on conventional cryptographic assumptions and were difficult to meet the requirements of post-quantum security, a periodically deniable ring signature scheme based on the Hamming quasi-cyclic (HQC) code-based cryptosystem was proposed. The scheme used the linear consistency relation induced by the HQC public key as the proof statement and constructed a non-interactive ring signature by combining a Stern-like Σ protocol, OR composition, and the Fiat-Shamir transformation. A time-window mechanism was introduced for periodic control of confirmation and disavowal. In the random oracle model, the scheme is proved secure based on support recovery and quasi-cyclic syndrome decoding decision problems, achieving unforgeability, anonymity, traceability, and non-slanderability. The analysis shows that the scheme achieves the unification of post-quantum sealrity, non-repucliation and periodic control with in the encooling framework.

title: COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF SVM AND IndoBERT FOR SENTIMENT ANALYSIS OF SAPAWARGA APPLICATION REVIEWS
abstract: The development of digital public services such as the Sapawarga application generates a large volume of user reviews, most of which are unstructured, making manual analysis inefficient. In addition, the use of mixed languages, including Sundanese and local slang, increases linguistic complexity that is difficult to handle using conventional methods. This study aims to compare the performance of Support Vector Machine (SVM) and IndoBERT using a dual-pipeline preprocessing approach to preserve data context. The dataset consists of 4,277 reviews classified into positive, negative, and neutral sentiments. The results show that IndoBERT outperforms SVM with an accuracy of 80.02% and an F1-Macro of 0.6517, while SVM achieves an accuracy of 75.82% and an F1-Macro of 0.6161. This advantage is supported by IndoBERT’s ability to understand context through self-attention and subword tokenization. This study supports the development of an automated public opinion monitoring system (Digital Ombudsman) for the Government of West Java to improve the quality of bureaucratic response.

title: Intellectual Property Challenges and Opportunities in Artificial Intelligence–Driven Innovation: An Empirical Assessment of Global and Indian Firms
abstract: This study analyses the emerging intellectual property (IP) challenges and opportunities arising from artificial intelligence (AI)–driven innovation, with a specific focus on comparative dynamics between global firms and Indian enterprises. Adopting an empirical research design, the study integrates secondary patent analytics with firm-level data and policy indicators. Quantitative techniques, including correlation and regression, are employed to assess the relationship and impact between AI adoption, IP strategies, and innovation outcomes. The results indicate that AI-intensive firms increasingly rely on hybrid IP strategies combining patents, trade secrets, and data governance mechanisms. While global firms demonstrate mature AI–IP integration, Indian firms exhibit rapid adaptation constrained by institutional and regulatory asymmetries. This research provides one of the few empirical assessments linking AI-driven innovation to IP strategy across developed and emerging economies, offering evidence-based insights for policymakers and corporate strategists.

title: The Role of AI in Navigating Disruptive Context
abstract: Disruptive technological change forces managers to make decisions under conditions of rapid change, ambiguity, and uncertainty. With the advance of AI and its ability to analyze vast amounts of data in mere seconds, decision-making has increasingly become a human–AI collaborative effort. Even with the growing evidence that AI can enhance analytical performance and pattern recognition, it remains unclear how AI performs in environments marked by complexity and uncertainty - core elements of strategic decision-making. Strategic decisions are challenging because they require forward-looking causal reasoning and timely action to navigate the uncertainty inherent in these environments. Yet, despite advances in AI research, we still lack an understanding of how AI interacts with managerial cognition, disruptive change, and strategic timing. This panel aims to clarify how managers recognize and respond to disruptive change, and to examine the role of AI in strategic decision-making, particularly in interpretation, timing, and action under uncertainty. By bringing together diverse scholars, this panel aims not only to be comprehensive but also to articulate a forward-looking research agenda.

title: Findable: A Biometric Measurement of Intimate Imagery Beyond the Reach of Ordinary Search
abstract: Content moderation for non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) is report-driven: material is removed when someone reports it. A report presupposes that the depicted person can find the material, and that prerequisite has, to our knowledge, never been measured. We measure it directly across four adult platforms. First, in 3,950 sampled clips (uniform random draws on three platforms, an uploader walk on the fourth), about half carry no name, alias, or production identifier in their metadata: no searchable person or production identifier is available. The locked classification pipeline finds 48.1% among the three uniformly sampled platforms and 56.1% in the observed four-platform sample after adding erome's non-uniform uploader walk; a model-blind reviewer-led audit (n = 400) and a recorded exact-model cross-provider pass bound the same quantities at 40.5–48.1% and 49.2–56.1%, so we report "about half" rather than a settled majority. Second, biometric face clustering of 2,497 encountered uploader catalogues, at a threshold calibrated on performer-labelled adult frames, shows that 90% of the 1,943 accounts crawled to assessable depth (at least 10 posts) depict ten or more biometrically distinct people; an inverse-multiplicity reweighting leaves the figure essentially unchanged (89.5%). Together the measurements identify a discovery gap: metadata search and account-by-account monitoring are unreliable routes to the measured content, so faster takedown cannot reach items that are never found. The claims concern discoverability, not consent, authorship, or total prevalence. The metadata measure does not establish that the depicted person knows the term, that the term is sufficiently specific, or that a search engine retrieves the clip. This is not an estimate of NCII prevalence; it measures discoverability-related properties of intimate imagery in the sampled platform content.
